params.body:
Guilherme's posts name their sources in the text ("Innova reports that 61% of Gen Z...", "In August 2026, Shopify reported...") but carry no links, and the Observatory's own corpus rarely holds the same facts: 64 of 78 live posts showed at most one source. Every named source was looked up, opened and checked against its sentence; this cites the ones that were verified, under the sentence that names them.

## Change

`bin/cite-sources.mjs <plan.json> --admitted-by=<person> [--run=<name>] [--dry]` and `--undo=<run>`. The plan: `[{article, sentence, url, publisher, page_title, date, passage}]`.
- Every page comes in under one source, "Cited by the author" (type editorial). The Standard has a person admit a source, never an engine: the first run needs `--admitted-by`, which is written on the source with the date.
- One signal per page: a page the Observatory already holds is reused by its address; a new one comes in with its title and the verified passage, and the pipeline classifies and enriches it like any other signal.
- Each citation is anchored to the sentence that names the source, with the note "cited by the author: <publisher>, <page title>, verified <date>". A sentence that is not in the post refuses the whole plan before anything is written; the same page is not cited twice on one post.
- `article_citation_undo` keeps the run; `--undo` takes the citations off and deletes the signals the run created (unless something else cites them by then).

## Checks

- `test/cite-sources.test.mjs` (4): refusals (no person to admit, sentence not in the post) write nothing; a dry run writes nothing; admission, signal, anchor and note; reuse of a known page; undo.
- Full suite 1225/1231; the 6 are `report-render` (`pdftoppm`, installed on the box).
- Dry run on a copy of production with the first plan: 101 verified citations over 48 posts, 100 new signals, 1 page already held.

Nothing runs at deploy. The plan file is handed over separately.
params.title: Cite the sources an author names, under the sentence that names them
